atoms.text: This guide configures Quillmark, a batch SQL query engine, to read Parquet files from the bucket acme-events-prod and write query results back to the same bucket. Quillmark scans input objects under the prefix events/parquet/ and writes result sets as compressed CSV files under the prefix query-results/. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Quillmark assumes, and the bucket policy is left unchanged. Create a role named quillmark-query-role and set its trust policy so that the Quillmark service principal, quillmark.svc.example.com, is permitted to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows GetObject and ListBucket on acme-events-prod, limited to the events/parquet/ prefix for reads. In the same policy, allow PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on the query-results/ prefix so that large result files can be uploaded in parts. Enter the role identifier in the Quillmark workspace settings so that each query session obtains temporary credentials from the role. Verify the setup by running a SELECT query over a small partition and confirming that the result file appears under query-results/ with the role session listed as the writer in the access logs.

This guide configures Quillmark, a batch SQL query engine, to read Parquet files from the bucket acme-events-prod and write query results back to the same bucket. Quillmark scans input objects under the prefix events/parquet/ and writes result sets as compressed CSV files under the prefix query-results/. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, and no IAM role is created. Open the bucket policy editor for acme-events-prod and add a statement whose Principal is the Quillmark service principal, quillmark.svc.example.com. Set that statement to allow GetObject and ListBucket, with resources limited to the events/parquet/ prefix for reads. In a second statement, allow PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on the query-results/ prefix so that large result files can be uploaded in parts. Enter only the bucket name in the Quillmark workspace settings so that each query session authenticates as the service principal itself. Verify the setup by running a SELECT query over a small partition and confirming that the result file appears under query-results/ with the service principal listed as the writer in the access logs.

This guide gives Tallyflow, a log compaction service, access to the bucket acme-logs-raw so that it can merge small log files into larger ones. Tallyflow reads gzip-compressed JSON log objects from the prefix incoming/ and writes compacted Parquet files to the prefix compacted/ every 15 minutes. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Tallyflow assumes, and the bucket policy is not modified. Create a role named tallyflow-compactor-role with a trust policy that allows the service principal tallyflow.svc.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that grants GetObject and ListBucket for incoming/ and PutObject for compacted/ in acme-logs-raw. Do not grant DeleteObject, because Tallyflow leaves source files in place and relies on a lifecycle rule for expiry. Set the role identifier in the Tallyflow pipeline definition so that every compaction run requests short-lived credentials for that role. After the first run, list compacted/ to confirm that Parquet files exist and check that the access log entries show the assumed-role session as the requester.

This guide connects Gridhaul, a nightly ETL job runner, to the bucket corp-etl-landing. The job starts at 02:00 UTC, reads CSV exports from the prefix finance-exports/, and writes cleansed output files and a job manifest to the prefix cleansed/. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Gridhaul assumes, and the bucket policy stays as it is. Create the role gridhaul-etl-role and configure its trust relationship to permit the service principal gridhaul.svc.example.com to assume it. Put the bucket permissions in the role's identity-based policy: GetObject and ListBucket on finance-exports/, and PutObject on cleansed/. Set the role identifier in the Gridhaul job definition so that the runner obtains temporary credentials at the start of each run. Limit the role session duration to two hours, which is longer than the longest observed run. To test, trigger a manual run against a one-day export and confirm that the manifest file is written to cleansed/ and that the access logs show the role session as the caller.

Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, and no IAM role is created. Add statements to the policy of corp-etl-landing that name the service principal gridhaul.svc.example.com as the Principal. Put the permissions in the bucket policy itself: GetObject and ListBucket on finance-exports/, and PutObject on cleansed/. Specify only the bucket name in the Gridhaul job definition so that the runner authenticates as its service principal at the start of each run. Because no assumed role is involved, no session duration needs to be configured. To test, trigger a manual run against a one-day export and confirm that the manifest file is written to cleansed/ and that the access logs show the service principal as the caller.

This guide authorizes Verity Scan, a file validation service, to work with the bucket partner-intake-prod. Verity Scan reads vendor files from the prefix vendor-drop/ and writes a JSON validation report for each file to the prefix reports/. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Verity Scan assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named verity-scan-role and set its trust policy to name the service principal verityscan.svc.example.com as the entity allowed to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows GetObject and ListBucket on vendor-drop/ and PutObject on reports/. The policy contains no write or delete actions for vendor-drop/, so original vendor files cannot be modified. Provide the role identifier in the Verity Scan project settings so that each validation task assumes the role before opening any objects. Upload a sample file to vendor-drop/ and wait for the scan task to finish. Confirm that a report named after the sample file appears in reports/ and that the request log records the role session as the principal.

This guide sets up Sumcast, an aggregation service, to compute daily rollups from hourly event files in the bucket metrics-store-eu. Sumcast reads hourly event objects from the prefix events/hourly/ and writes one aggregate file per day to the prefix daily-rollups/. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Sumcast assumes, and the bucket policy is left untouched. Create a role named sumcast-rollup-role with a trust policy that lets the service principal sumcast.svc.example.com assume it. Add an identity-based policy to the role with GetObject and ListBucket for events/hourly/ and with PutObject for daily-rollups/ in metrics-store-eu. Include a condition in the role policy that restricts requests to the bucket's region, so the role cannot be used against replicas elsewhere. Configure the Sumcast schedule with the role identifier so that each rollup task requests credentials for the role. Run a backfill for one past day and compare the object count in the rollup file with the source hours. Check that the access log shows the assumed-role session as the writer of the rollup object.

This guide allows Sessionly, a clickstream sessionization service, to process data in the bucket web-analytics-prod. Sessionly reads raw clickstream objects from the prefix clickstream/raw/ and writes sessionized records, split into parts of up to 128 MB, to the prefix sessions/. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Sessionly assumes, and no change is made to the bucket policy. Create a role named sessionly-processor-role and add a trust policy naming the service principal sessionly.svc.example.com as allowed to assume it. In the role's identity-based policy, allow GetObject and ListBucket on clickstream/raw/. In the same policy, allow PutObject, AbortMultipartUpload, and ListBucketMultipartUploads on sessions/, because the output parts are uploaded using multipart transfers. Enter the role identifier in the Sessionly processor configuration so that each worker assumes the role when it starts. Start the processor on one hour of data and watch the worker logs for access denied errors. When the run finishes, confirm that the part files in sessions/ are complete and that the requester in the access log is the role session.

This guide gives Plotline, a scheduled notebook runner, access to the bucket research-datasets. Each Plotline job reads input datasets from the prefix datasets/ and writes the executed notebook and its output tables to a per-run folder under the prefix job-output/. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Plotline assumes, and the bucket policy is not edited. Create a role named plotline-runner-role and write its trust policy so that the service principal plotline.svc.example.com may assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows GetObject and ListBucket on datasets/ and PutObject on job-output/ in research-datasets. Add no permissions on other buckets, since the notebooks only use data stored in research-datasets. Set the role identifier as the execution identity in the Plotline workspace so that each scheduled job runs with temporary credentials from that role. Schedule a test notebook that reads one small dataset and writes a single table. After it completes, verify that the run folder exists in job-output/ and that the access log lists the role session as the requester.

This guide configures Lakeprobe, an interactive query service, to use the bucket analytics-curated. Lakeprobe reads curated tables stored as ORC files under the prefix curated/ and writes intermediate spill files and final result sets to the prefix query-scratch/, which has a lifecycle rule that expires objects after seven days. Access is granted only through an IAM role that Lakeprobe assumes, and the bucket policy is not modified. Create a role named lakeprobe-query-role and set its trust policy to allow the service principal lakeprobe.svc.example.com to assume it. Define the bucket permissions in the role's identity-based policy: GetObject and ListBucket on curated/, and PutObject and GetObject on query-scratch/. The GetObject permission on query-scratch/ is required because Lakeprobe reads its own spill files back during large joins. Register the role identifier as the query execution role in the Lakeprobe console. Run a join across two curated tables and check that spill files appear in query-scratch/ while the query is running. Review the access log to confirm that all requests came from the role session.
